Installing Linux Mint on a windows PC

Depending on the system, make sure there is enough room on the hard drive to install Mint.

If you want mostly standard Mint, that would be about 20-25GB, but I would probably say with additions and room for testing, have 100GB of free space.

I don't know if the windows you are on has a defrag - but you could try that to get the space freed up in a nice size block too.

If there is any doubt about trying to resize the windows partition, you could try to create another partition in windows, and then use that one for Mint. Backup any data that is important - as always.

Alternately, just adding a second hard drive with Mint on it would be a very good option - 120GB ssd for under $25 is workable, and 250GB drives are also very economical.

As for what you need during the install, I would say not very much. Drivers should be installed automatically and support for most older hardware is very good.

Okay. I remember when I first installed it, I ran into so many obstacles. Current HD is a TB SSD so space shouldn't be too much of an issue.

I will probably be posting in this sub verse a bunch of dumb questions.

TB is a good size. If windows has splattered files all around, defrag might be needed, but backup if you use the Mint "resize windows partition" option.
Personally, I always use new ssd drives for all my Linux installs, and rotate through if I reinstall a new distro.

I always advocate installation on a separate drive, just for safety sake. New drives are inexpensive, and that way there is zero chance of making a mistake of breaking anything during the install. Pull out your Windows drive, pop in the new drive and install the new OS on it, in this case Mint. After you get Mint installed and up and running, shut down and put the Windows drive back in and set the startup drive to your Linux Mint drive in your BIOS/EFI. When you boot back into Mint, run the following command, "sudo update-grub". This will let the linux bootloader (Grub) detect the windows install. So the next time you boot up, you will get a window that lets you select between booting into Mint or Windows without having to switch boot drives in the BIOS/EFI.

It is possible to do it with a current existing windows, but it's messy if your not careful because of how the windows partition manager works. My suggestion is to defrag, get a partition tool, partition the drive in windows, defrag one more time to be safe, then attempt the Linux install. Installing Linux after windows will allow the grub to enable dual boot, but you gotta be really careful with the data or it could be lost in the install. Beyond that it shouldn't be bad.

If possible, I'd do a fresh windows install if it's feasible. If not, defrag the fuck out of it and cross your fingers
